A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PixWizard research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original PixWizard benchmark evaluations, generated examples, and component and training ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark evaluations and ablations and adds a qualitative guidance-weight experiment in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: The flow-based DiT, encoders, structural and semantic guidance, task-aware sampler, arbitrary-resolution handling, and two-stage training procedure are retained. The new MHGS pseudocode and expanded resolution explanation document existing components rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The named datasets and benchmark tasks are retained. However, v3 removes flash-reflection removal from Section 2's training-task list while retaining its Flash Remove instruction templates in Figure 10. Whether this represents an actual reduction in training coverage is unresolved.

E2.justification: V3 adds CRIS to the referring-segmentation comparison in Table 6, corresponding to v1 Table 5. Comparator membership in the other benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 revises the reported sketch training pairs from 0.5M to 0.4M and pose pairs from 0.4M to 0.25M; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. The new guidance experiment varies image weights over 1, 2, and 3 and text weights over 4, 7.5, and 14 for Canny-to-image generation and depth estimation.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 and Figure 12 add a classifier-free guidance sensitivity analysis examining saturation and depth-estimation failures. The structural/semantic guidance, token-sampling, and two-stage-training ablations already existed in v1 Appendix D.3 and are relocated to v3 Section 4.4.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same HPSv2 uncertainty reporting, including PixWizard's 27.47 ± 0.183. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises PixWizard's SUNRGB-D RMSE from 0.288 to 0.291 and ADE20K mIoU from 36.76 to 32.76. Direct-mask grounding results change, including gRefCOCO 34.17 to 29.07 and RefCOCO validation 46.44 to 44.38; several ablation scores also change. CRIS results and guidance/inpainting examples are added. Most benchmark values remain unchanged, but v3 Table 1 still reports RefCOCO validation as 46.44, conflicting with Table 6.

T1.justification: The eight numbered equations and flow-matching preliminaries are retained. There are no added or revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations; the new sampler pseudocode provides implementation detail.

C1.justification: The central assistant, dataset, architecture, and generalization contributions remain. The introduction narrows competitiveness against specialists to certain tasks and superiority over generalists to most tasks. Section 2 also removes the claim that the dataset is the largest and most diverse.

C2.justification: V3 adds task-dependent guidance interpretations: stronger image guidance can oversaturate outputs and suppress depth variation, while stronger text guidance can damage dense prediction. It removes the attribution of inpainting quality to blank-canvas training and the former inference-efficiency explanation. The existing multi-image-input and specialist-performance limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds MHGS pseudocode with temperature and token-count defaults, plus patch-selection, padding, and attention-mask details. It removes the shifted-schedule, Heun/Midpoint, and 30–60-NFE discussion, the explicit 30,000 Places crops and rightward outpainting direction, and the text-to-image data-source sentence. The code/resource link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to Palette, Image Super-Resolution via Iterative Refinement, CRIS, and Guo et al. (2025) on reasoning in image generation. The broader diffusion-model and vision-generalist positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: ablations move into the main text, while task-embedding visualization, arbitrary-resolution details, evaluation procedures, and precise-editing workflows move into dedicated appendix sections. Numerous method and results paragraphs are condensed or rewritten, and acknowledgements and author information are updated.

P2.justification: V3 substantially rearranges the displays, moving the ablation table into the main text and the t-SNE and precise-editing figures into the appendix. Figure 9 combines outpainting and text-to-image examples with new inpainting examples, and Figure 12 adds a guidance grid. Table 3's caption and score emphasis are revised, and the grounding table gains a CRIS row.

improvement.justification: The guidance sensitivity analysis, sampler pseudocode, expanded resolution explanation, and narrower claims improve documentation and calibration. However, v3 introduces an unresolved RefCOCO validation discrepancy between Tables 1 and 6 and removes specific inference and evaluation details. These gains and reporting weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
